title: The brief, the options and the review come back from the tool as text the human can read in the chat
description: Today write_brief returns only '<node> has a brief. Show it to the human…' (packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts ~466), so the agent has to rebuild the brief itself and often just points at the board. Add a renderBrief(node, brief) to packages/mcp/src/render.ts: title, approach, and every acceptance criterion (command + what passing proves). Return it from write_brief and from the brief tool. Check renderDecisions gives every option with label, reason and costLater, and renderReview the findings and criteria — fill whatever is missing. End each block with one line: 'Paste this above the question before you ask.' Test: snapshot/unit tests next to render.ts covering a brief with two criteria and a decision with three options. Scope follows the relay decision: under prose-only this node shrinks to only checking what renderDecisions/renderReview already carry.

brief.approach:
Score 3: the node is smaller than its own text expects, because two of the three renderers are already right and `core` already owns the third. The work is one return value and one line of prose in three places — plus resisting the second renderer the node's text asks for.

**Read before writing: the node's text is out of date on one point.** It says to add a `renderBrief(node, brief)` to `packages/mcp/src/render.ts`. Do not. `core` already exports `renderBrief(board, id)` (`packages/core/src/brief.ts`), it renders the title, the complexity line, the approach, the acceptance list, the project, the decisions and the declared files, and the `brief` tool at `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:422` already returns it whole. A second brief renderer in `mcp` is exactly the two-places-to-keep-in-step cost the accepted decision already warns about, doubled for no gain. Use the one that exists.

**1. `write_brief` returns the brief, not a pointer to it.** Its handler (`plan.ts`, the `registerTool('write_brief', …)` block) ends with `text('<node> has a brief. Show it to the human…')`. After `writeBrief` returns, `loadBoard` and call `renderBrief(board, node)`, and return that followed by the existing instruction sentence. That is the whole mechanical half: the agent no longer has to rebuild the brief from what it just sent, and cannot fall back to pointing at the board.

**2. The one line, in three places.** Each block that a human is meant to read before being asked something ends with a single line: `Paste this above the question before you ask.` It goes at the end of

- the new `write_brief` reply (before approval),
- `renderDecisions` in `packages/mcp/src/render.ts:86` (before a `decide`),
- `renderReview` in the same file (before an `accept`).

For `renderDecisions`, put it only on the non-empty path — the `'Nothing is waiting on you.'` return has nothing to paste. Exact same wording in all three; a line that varies is a line people stop recognising.

**3. Check the other two carry their fields, and change nothing that already does.** Verified in the tree today, so this is a confirmation step, not a rewrite: `renderDecisions` (line 93-101) emits `id`, `label`, `because: reason` and `later: costLater` for every option, with a comment saying neither half is ever dropped (ADR 0024), plus `Suggested:`. `renderReview` emits the scan result, every finding with file and line, the uncommitted-file warning, the CI line and the criteria. Both are complete. If something is genuinely missing, add it; do not restructure either function to look like the other.

**4. Tests** beside `render.ts` — `packages/mcp/src/render.test.ts` if it exists, otherwise create it next to the module. Two cases the node asks for: a decision with three options renders all three with `because` and `later` for each and ends with the paste line; and a review renders its findings and criteria and ends with the same line. For the brief, assert through the tool rather than the renderer, in `test/integration/mcp.test.ts`: `write_brief` with two criteria returns a reply containing both commands and both `proves` strings — which is the behaviour change, and testing it at the tool is what proves the agent receives it.

Nothing outside `packages/mcp` changes. `core`'s `renderBrief` is not edited, the CLI is not touched, and no skill is rewritten here — the instructions half of the accepted decision is already in the brief and decide skills, which say to put the text in front of the user before asking.

acceptance.proves: a decision renders every option with its reason and what it costs later, a review renders its findings and criteria, and both end with the paste line a human is meant to see
write_brief now returns the rendered brief itself — both commands and both `proves` strings come back — so the agent relays it instead of rebuilding it or pointing at the board

acceptance.run: test "$(git grep -c 'Paste this above the question before you ask' -- packages/mcp/src | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = '2' && git grep -q 'Paste this above the question before you ask' -- packages/mcp/src/render.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts
acceptance.proves: the same sentence, word for word, ends all three blocks — a wording that varies between them is one people stop recognising

acceptance.run: ! git grep -q 'renderBrief' -- packages/mcp/src/render.ts && git grep -q 'renderBrief' -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts
acceptance.proves: core's existing renderBrief was reused rather than a second brief renderer being written in mcp — the duplication the accepted decision's cost line warns about
only the MCP package and its integration test changed: core, the schema, the CLI, the dashboard and every skill are untouched
the widened write_brief reply compiles against the real Board and Brief types
